lead: Hayward plumbing deals with an active fault line, soft water and 1950s and 1960s slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Hayward.
risk: slab leaks, earthquake-related line damage and water heater strapping
risk_short: slab leaks, quake damage and water heaters
why: Much of Hayward was built in the 1950s and 1960s, so many homes have copper or galvanized lines under the slab that now leak. The Hayward Highlands and Fairview are a mix of older and newer homes.
The Hayward Fault runs right through downtown and slowly creeps, bending curbs and buried pipes. Strapped water heaters and flexible gas connectors matter here.
water: Hayward buys all of its water from the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission's Hetch Hetchy system. It is very soft.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Keep a wrench by your gas shutoff.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Check for leaks after any strong quake.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Hayward, the Hayward Highlands, Fairview, Mt. Eden, Tennyson-Alquire, Southgate and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Hayward Building Division, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.q: Does the Hayward Fault affect home plumbing?
faq.a: It can. The fault slowly creeps through the city, and a large quake could break lines. Homes near the fault should have strapped water heaters, flexible gas connectors and known shutoff locations.
